stories.title: User Signs In
stories.prompt: What happens when a user signs in?
stories.goal: to access the application with their account
stories.benefit: their identity, session, and access level are established before they continue
conversation: Sign-in starts from an existing users row; account creation and password reset are outside this story.
The schema stores the active login in sessions and derives access context from user_roles and roles.
permissions is an action catalog without declared role links in this sample, so it is useful context but not part of the authenticated relation path.

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing account with valid credentials
acceptance_criteria.when: the user submits the sign-in form
acceptance_criteria.then: the matching users row is found by email and its password_hash can be verified
a sessions row is created for that users.id with an expires_at timestamp

acceptance_criteria.given: the signed-in user has assigned roles
acceptance_criteria.when: the app loads the authenticated context
acceptance_criteria.then: user_roles links the user to roles that describe their access level

playback.text: The sign-in attempt begins by finding the existing account in users, using email as the login identifier and password_hash for credential verification.
After the account is verified, the new session is attached to users.id so later requests can resolve the session token back to the signed-in account.
Authorization context fans out through user_roles, which uses the same users.id identity anchor to find each role assignment.
Each role assignment resolves to roles, giving the app named access levels for the authenticated user.
With the session token active and roles loaded, the app can treat the request as signed in and apply permission checks from the available access catalog.
